items.prompt: A signed-in user who may not view website w1 calls GET /api/websites/w1/pageviews with a valid date range. What status comes back?
items.answer: 401, since the route answers unauthorized() here
distractors: 403, since the route answers forbidden() for this case
404, so that the website id is not disclosed
200 with empty pageviews and sessions arrays
items.explanation: The pageviews route returns unauthorized() when canViewWebsite is false, so the status is 401 even for a signed-in user. There is no forbidden() call and no empty-result fallback in this route.

items.prompt: A dashboard query fails once because the API returned a 500. With the QueryClient defaults in Providers.tsx, what does React Query do?
items.answer: It reports the error at once, as retry is false
distractors: It retries 3 times with backoff, the library default
It retries one time after the one-minute stale time
It keeps retrying until the window regains focus
items.explanation: Providers creates the QueryClient with retry: false, so a failed query goes straight to the error state; the library default of 3 retries is overridden. The other two defaults are refetchOnWindowFocus: false and staleTime of one minute.

items.prompt: A user leaves the dashboard tab for five minutes, then switches back to it. What does React Query do on that focus?
items.answer: Nothing, as refetchOnWindowFocus is set to false
distractors: It refetches, as the one-minute staleTime is over
It refetches every query in the cache at that time
It clears the cache and reloads the whole page
items.explanation: Even though the data is older than the one-minute staleTime, Providers sets refetchOnWindowFocus: false, so focusing the tab does not trigger a refetch. Stale data is refetched on the next mount or explicit invalidation instead.

items.prompt: MetricCard receives value 120 and change 20. What percent change does it compute?
distractors: 16.7%, because 20 is divided by the current 120
120%, because the value is divided by the change
-20%, as change is subtracted from the value
items.explanation: diff = value - change = 100 is the previous value, and pct = ((value - diff) / diff) * 100 = (20 / 100) * 100 = 20. The caller passes the delta as change, not the previous value.

items.prompt: MetricCard receives value 50 and change 50, so the previous period was 0. What percent change does it show?
items.answer: 100, the fallback for a zero base and nonzero value
distractors: Infinity, from dividing 50 by a previous value of 0
0, the fallback whenever the previous value is zero
NaN, which the spring animation then renders as 0
items.explanation: diff is 0, so the ternary skips the division: diff !== 0 is false and value !== 0 is true, giving 100. Only when both diff and value are 0 does pct become 0.

items.prompt: A client calls GET /api/websites?includeTeams=false. Which websites does the route return?
items.answer: The user and team websites, since "false" is truthy
distractors: Only the user's own websites, as the flag is false
A 400 error, because includeTeams must be boolean
Only team websites, as the flag inverts the filter
items.explanation: includeTeams is declared as z.string().optional(), so the value is the string "false". The route checks if (query.includeTeams), and any non-empty string is truthy, so it calls getAllUserWebsitesIncludingTeamOwner. Only omitting the parameter gives the user-only list.

items.prompt: POST /api/websites is called with a teamId the caller may create websites in. Which owner fields does the new website row get?
items.answer: The team id plus createdBy; no userId is stored
distractors: The caller as userId, and the team id is dropped
All three: userId, teamId and the createdBy field
Only the team id; the creator is not recorded
items.explanation: data always has createdBy: auth.user.id and teamId; data.userId is set only if (!teamId). A team website is therefore owned by the team, and canViewWebsite later checks team membership for it.

items.prompt: POST /api/websites includes shareId "acme-public". What else happens besides creating the website?
items.answer: A share row with slug acme-public is created for it
distractors: shareId is saved as a column on the website row
shareId is ignored until the share API is called
The website is made public by setting a flag on it
items.explanation: When shareId is present, the route calls createShare with entityId set to the website id, shareType website, the website name, slug: shareId and overview/events parameters, then returns the website with shareId set to the share slug.

items.prompt: In CLOUD_MODE, a user with no subscription who already has the maximum number of personal websites posts a new one without teamId. What comes back?
items.answer: 401 with the message Website limit reached.
distractors: 402 Payment Required, with an upgrade link
403 Forbidden, from canCreateWebsite failing
200, with the site created in a disabled state
items.explanation: The CLOUD_MODE branch counts the user's websites and, at CLOUD_WEBSITE_LIMIT, returns unauthorized({ message: "Website limit reached." }), a 401. The permission checks come after this branch.

items.prompt: CLICKHOUSE_URL is set, and a query object passed to runQuery has prisma, clickhouse and kafka entries. Which one runs?
items.answer: The kafka entry, checked first under ClickHouse
distractors: The clickhouse entry, as Kafka is write-only
The prisma entry, since DATABASE_URL is set as well
Both clickhouse and kafka, one after the other
items.explanation: With CLICKHOUSE_URL set, runQuery returns queries[KAFKA]() if that entry exists and queries[CLICKHOUSE]() otherwise. Exactly one function runs, and PostgreSQL is only considered when CLICKHOUSE_URL is absent.

items.prompt: CLICKHOUSE_URL is unset and DATABASE_URL starts with mysql://. What does runQuery return for an analytics query?
items.answer: undefined, as only postgresql is wired to Prisma
distractors: The prisma result, as Prisma serves every SQL URL
An error thrown by notImplemented() for MySQL
The clickhouse result, used as the default path
items.explanation: getDatabaseType maps postgres to postgresql and returns other schemes as-is, so mysql stays "mysql". runQuery only calls queries[PRISMA]() for postgresql and has no other branch, so the function falls through and returns undefined.

items.prompt: The app is built with basePath "/analytics". Which URL does useApi().get("/websites/w1/pageviews") request?
items.answer: The base path first, then /api, then the given path
distractors: /api first, ignoring the configured base path entirely
The base path and the given path, with no /api segment
An absolute https URL built from the server hostname
items.explanation: getUrl leaves absolute http URLs alone and otherwise returns basePath + "/api" + url, so the base path comes first and /api second. Without a basePath the prefix is just /api.

items.prompt: A signed-in user who also holds a share token in the app store browses /websites/w1 (not a /share page). Which headers does useApi send?
items.answer: The Authorization bearer header, but no share headers
distractors: Both share headers, plus the Authorization header too
Only the share token header, with no bearer token sent
No headers at all, since cookies carry the session
items.explanation: Share headers (token and context) are added only when the pathname starts with /share and a share token exists. The Authorization: Bearer header from getClientAuthToken() is always part of defaultHeaders.

items.front: Trace the website pageviews chart from component to storage.
items.back: WebsiteChart reads timezone and date range; useWebsitePageviewsQuery builds the query key and calls /websites/:id/pageviews through useApi (bearer and share headers, /api prefix); the route runs parseRequest, canViewWebsite (401 if not), getQueryFilters, then getPageviewStats and getSessionStats in parallel, which dispatch through runQuery to Prisma or ClickHouse.

items.front: What are the QueryClient defaults in Providers.tsx, and what do they mean?
items.back: retry: false (a failed query errors immediately), refetchOnWindowFocus: false (focusing the tab never refetches), staleTime: 60 seconds (data counts as fresh for a minute, so remounts within that time use the cache).

items.front: How does POST /api/websites decide who owns a new website?
items.back: createdBy is always the caller. With a teamId (after canCreateTeamWebsite passes) the website belongs to the team and userId is not set; without one, userId is the caller. In CLOUD_MODE personal websites are capped for users without a subscription.
